THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, UMESH M. ADIGA J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
This appeal is filed by the claimant in MVC No.230/2016 on the file of MACT, Raichur, being aggrieved by the in the Judgment and award dated 20.06.2017, for enhancement of compensation.
2. Parties will be referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.

3. It was the case of the petitioner before the MACT that on 11.12.2015 at about 06.00 a.m., he met with an accident on NH-44 road at Dupadu village due to rash and negligent driving of Mini Lorry bearing No. AP-21/W-0098 by its driver and due to the same he sustained fractures of right and left forearms, left radius and ulna, left humerus, left femur and injuries to the chest.
He had taken treatment in Sparsha Hospital, Bangalore, under went two surgeries and spent lot of money for treatment.
He further contended that he was aged about 23 years at the time of accident and was earning `825/- per day by working as a mason at Bangalore.
He has been suffering from permanent disability to an extent of 43% for whole body as assessed by treated doctor.
With these reasons, he prayed to award compensation of `54,54,600/-.
4. Respondents had contended that amount of compensation claimed was on higher side and denied other averments of petition.
Respondent No.2 had taken contention that the driver of mini lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-21/W-0098 was not holding valid and effective driving licence.
Owner had violated the terms and conditions of the policy and prayed to dismissal.
5. On the basis of pleadings, Tribunal had framed necessary issues.
6. The petitioner had examined PW1 to PW3 and got marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P31.
Respondent No.2 had examined RW1 and got marked Ex.R1 to Ex.R7.
7. The learned MACT on appreciating the evidence on record awarded the following compensation.

Pain and suffering : `60,000/-

In total `13,93,414/- was awarded with interest at the rate of 6% per annum and directed both the respondents to pay the compensation, by impugned judgment and award.
8. With the consent of the learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for the respondent No.2, the matter is taken up for final disposal at the stage of admission.
9. We have heard the arguments of learned counsels for both the parties.

10. The following point emerges for determination:
"Whether the appellant is entitled for enhancement of compensation?
11. The learned counsel for the petitioner vehemently contended that petitioner had sustained several fractures.
He underwent several operations in Sparsha Hospital, Bangalore which is Multi Specialty Hospital.

The Medical Officer had been examined in this case, who had corroborated the case of the petitioner and opined that the petitioner has been suffering from permanent disability to an extent of 43% of the whole body.
However, learned Trial Judge has not considered the said disability and determined the disability as 20% to the whole body.
The petitioner was serving as mason and earning `825/- per day.
Petitioner had produced relevant documents in this regard and examined owner of the said construction company.
However, the MACT did not accept the same and notional income of the petitioner was taken as `8,000/- per month, which is highly erroneous.
Even amount of compensation awarded under the other heads are also on the lower side.
With these reasons sought to enhance amount of compensation.
12. The learned counsel for respondent No.2 has contended that the Tribunal has considered the case properly and awarded just and reasonable compensation and does not call for any interference.

The MACT in detail discussed regarding the income of the petitioner, permanent disability and other factors to be considered to award the compensation and hence prayed to reject the appeal.
13.
The Presiding Officer of the MACT assessed the evidence on record about income of the petitioner at para 22 and rightly rejected the said contention by valid reasons.
The said finding of the MACT does not call for any inference.

Therefore, the income of the petitioner as determined by Mohammed Rafi vs The General Manager And Anr on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122393301/
3 the Tribunal at the rate of `8,000/- per month is just and proper.

sentences.text: The Tribunal has not added future prospects to the income of the petitioner.
According to the findings of the MACT, age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 29 years.

In the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157, Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that (even in case of the person who is self employed or fixed income)
future prospects of victims has to be considered and if the age of victim/ injured is less than 40 years, then 40% of the income has to be added towards future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this case, age of victim was 29 years and hence 40% of income was to be added towards future prospects.
If same is added, then the income of petitioner per month is `11,200/-.
14. The MACT in para 24 of impugned judgment appreciated evidence and held that claimant was suffering by permanent disability to an extent of 20% of the whole body.
From the material available, the Tribunal had taken the percentage of permanent disability at lower side.
The treated and expert doctor had opined that petitioner has been suffering from permanent disability to the whole body at 43%.
Considering the other factors such as age of the petitioner, speedy recovery of fractures etc., the permanent disability of the petitioner is taken as 30% of the whole body.
It is not in dispute that the multiplier applicable to the age of the petitioner is 17.
On the basis of the said calculation, compensation under the head of loss of future earning capacity due to permanent disability is to be recalculated.

15. As rightly submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant/petitioner, the amount of compensation awarded under the head of pain and suffering, attendant charges, loss of earning during laid up period, and loss of amenities are on lower side and have to be recalculated and re-assessed.

16. The contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner that according to the evidence of PW2 minimum `3,00,000/- is required for future medical expenses, however the Tribunal has awarded `1,00,000/- towards future medical expenses is not tenable.
The assessment of PW2 regarding medical expenses is only on the basis of assumption and presumption without any material.
Petitioner had not produced quotation of hospital for the said treatment before the Tribunal for calculation of the said amount.
Hence not considered.
17. For assessment of compensation under the head of loss of earning during laid up period, income without adding future prospects has to be taken into account and hence it has to recalculated.
The Tribunal assessed the attendant charges at the rate of `100/- per day.
Which is on lower side.
The petitioner had sustained fractures of both the hands as well as fracture of the left - 10 - femur.
Under these circumstances, he might be dependent on attendant to do his ordinary pursuits when he was in-patient in the hospital and even after discharged from the hospital for few months.
Therefore attendant charges is considered as `5,000/- per month and for a period of six months he might have taken attendant, which needs to be compensated.
Similarly for a period of about six months be might not be able to work and earn and lost his income.

 Pain and suffering : `.75,000/-

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of `18,42,454/- as against `13,93,414/- awarded by the - 11 - Tribunal and he is entitled for enhancement of `4,49,040/-.

The petitioner is also entitled for interest on the enhanced amount of compensation at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till payment of enhanced amount of compensation.
19.

For the aforesaid discussion, we answer the point accordingly and pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is partly allowed, with costs.
ii. The impugned judgment and award dated 20.06.2017 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Raichur in MVC No.230/2016 is modified.
`18,42,454/- is awarded as compensation as against `13,93,414/- awarded by the MACT.
The petitioner is entitled for enhanced compensation of `4,48,600/- with future interest at the rate of 6% per annum on the enhanced amount from the date of petition till realization of the amount.
Respondent No.2 is directed to pay the  said amount within six weeks from  receipt of copy of award.
